words.gloss_range: an indefinite boy/youth predicate; the range can include a vulnerable young male and, contextually, one reducible toward slave-boy status
words.prose: {{ar:غُلَامٌ}} ({{tr:ghulāmun}}) classifies the visible referent as a boy or youth without naming him. Its indefinite predicate form makes him a category in the discoverer's mouth, and the word's range leaves vulnerable youth and possible servile reduction in view. That is why the glad-tidings pairing feels inverted: a boy-word familiar from announcement scenes such as 19:19, 15:53, and 51:28 becomes the first step toward commodification.
words.root_gloss_range: boy, youth, young servant or slave-boy possibilities; locally an indefinite nominal predicate after the demonstrative

topics.headline: indefinite nominal classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph is first named by category, not by identity.
topics.reason: The indefinite nominative predicate completes the demonstrative nominal clause and classifies the visible referent.

topics.headline: youth vulnerability range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees both the promise of youth and the vulnerability that lets the scene reduce him toward sale.
topics.reason: The local noun permits a boy/youth range, and the following merchandise clause gives the possible slave-boy pressure narrative relevance.

topics.headline: announcement pairing inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a boy announced elsewhere as gift or wonder, such as 19:19, 15:53, and 51:28, is here discovered accidentally and categorized for trade.
topics.reason: Parallels such as 19:19, 15:53, 51:28, and 18:74 sharpen contrast, but the local clause remains a discoverers identification, not a birth announcement.

words.gloss_range: connector pivoting from discovery speech into concealment
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the discovery cry to the morally charged concealment clause without naming a fresh subject. It can coordinate and resume at once, so the narrative turns from public delight into hidden treatment of Joseph as property.

topics.headline: discovery to concealment pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse does not pause between finding the boy and hiding him as merchandise.
topics.reason: The connector licenses continuation or resumption before the concealment verb and keeps the subject implicit.

words.gloss_range: they concealed him, with plural subject ambiguity and an object suffix keeping Joseph unnamed
words.prose: {{ar:أَسَرُّوهُ}} ({{tr:asarrūhu}}) reverses the public cry into secrecy. The plural subject can point to the caravan group or remain broad enough to keep multiple actors under suspicion, and the attached object suffix hides Joseph by grammar even as he has just been pointed out. The root's conceal/disclose tension is locally narrowed to concealment because {{ar:بِضَاعَةً}} ({{tr:biḍāʿatan}}) names the state in which they hide him, and the final divine knowledge clause answers that secrecy directly.
words.root_gloss_range: secrecy, concealment, and in some uses disclosure or making known; locally Form IV with object suffix selects concealment after public discovery

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the commodity state that follows the concealment verb

topics.headline: ambiguous plural concealers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar keeps the concealing group plural and not fully individualized.
topics.reason: The masculine plural verb can continue from the caravan members, while the connector and narrative context keep subject scope live.

topics.headline: public cry to secrecy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the scene snap from announced joy into a completed act of concealment.
topics.reason: The root has conceal/disclose antinomy, but the local transitive clause and following merchandise state select concealment after the public cry.

topics.headline: concealment and sale thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this hidden possession points forward to sale in 12:20 and later hidden knowledge in 12:77.
topics.reason: The rows connect this object-suffixed concealment to the sale action in 12:20 and to same-surah concealment at 12:77, while divine knowing remains the immediate local answer.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative commodity state, functioning circumstantially for the hidden human object
words.prose: {{ar:بِضَاعَةً}} ({{tr:biḍāʿatan}}) lands the concealment clause by classifying Joseph in the state of merchandise. The accusative ḥāl reading is crucial: they hid him while treating him as goods. The cut-portion root image makes the commodity label feel like severance from family, but the local noun names the market status, and later Surah 12 trade-goods scenes at 12:62, 12:65, and 12:88 return to the same plot economy.
words.root_gloss_range: goods, merchandise, trade property, with an underlying cut/portion field; local noun names commodity status rather than the act of cutting

topics.headline: commodity ḥāl grammar
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that merchandise is not merely an object label but Josephs contemporaneous state in the concealment act.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence supports the accusative as circumstantial ḥāl describing the concealed object.

topics.headline: human commodification and cut image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the moral violence of a human referent being put into a goods category, with severance pressure behind the word.
topics.reason: The cut-root image is useful as pressure, but local form evidence keeps the selected sense as commodity/goods rather than the cutting action itself.

topics.headline: surah trade economy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Josephs first commodity label becomes part of the surahs later trade-goods vocabulary at 12:62, 12:65, and 12:88.
topics.reason: The same merchandise root returns in Surah 12 trade scenes such as 12:62, 12:65, and 12:88, while 12:42 is a different few-years use of the root field.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector introducing the divine commentary clause
words.prose: This {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the closing divine comment rather than another ordinary action in the chain. It links the concealment clause to a narrator-level frame: human secrecy is immediately enclosed by divine knowledge.

topics.headline: divine commentary connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from narrated human action to divine evaluation without losing continuity.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the final nominal clause with the concealment clause and introduces the ayahs closing frame.

words.gloss_range: the explicit divine proper-name subject of the nominal knowledge clause
words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) makes God, not the plural human actors, the subject of the closing knowledge clause. The proper name stands outside the past-tense action chain as a nominal frame, and after 12:18's appeal for divine help it answers hidden commodification with direct divine presence and knowledge. The God-plus-knowing formula recurs across Surah 12, including 12:21, 12:40, 12:68, 12:76, 12:83, and 12:96, but here it is specialized as surveillance over concealment.
words.root_gloss_range: divine name with worship/refuge/bewilderment etymological discussions; locally the proper name is the definite subject specified by knowing

topics.headline: explicit divine subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source of knowledge is explicitly God, not any human witness.
topics.reason: The proper divine name is nominative subject of a nominal clause whose predicate is the knowledge adjective.

topics.headline: divine frame after help appeal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the story move from Jacobs appeal to God in 12:18 to Gods knowing of hidden human action in 12:19.
topics.reason: The prior boundary gives a concrete divine-reliance frame, and the local clause specializes it through knowledge after concealment.

topics.headline: God-knowing formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a widespread God-plus-knowing formula, recurring in Surah 12 at 12:21, 12:40, 12:68, 12:76, 12:83, and 12:96, that is made local by its placement after concealment.
topics.reason: Cooccurrence rows and root-dispute material are broad provenance; locally the proper name functions as the subject of the knowledge predicate, with formula recurrences such as 12:21, 12:40, 12:68, 12:76, 12:83, and 12:96 as background.

words.gloss_range: indefinite intensive qualitative predicate: fully knowing with respect to what they do
words.prose: {{ar:عَلِيمٌ}} ({{tr:ʿalīmun}}) is not a passing act of knowing but an intensive qualitative predicate: God is fully knowing with respect to their deeds. Its indefiniteness and faʿīl form make the attribute stable and comprehensive, answering {{ar:أَسَرُّوهُ}} ({{tr:asarrūhu}}) with the opposite pressure of complete knowledge. The formula is familiar from Surah 12 knowledge closures such as 12:50 and 12:83, but here it lands precisely after concealment and merchandise.
words.root_gloss_range: knowledge, knowing, teaching, and the knowable realm; local faʿīl adjective expresses intensive stable knowledge

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the concealment verb answered by the divine knowledge predicate

topics.headline: intensive qualitative predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause attributes comprehensive, stable knowing rather than a one-time awareness.
topics.reason: The indefinite faʿīl predicate of the definite divine subject supports an intensive qualitative reading.

topics.headline: knowledge counters secrecy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees concealment become unstable because the hidden act is already inside divine knowledge.
topics.reason: The attribute follows the concealment clause and directly counters secrecy with comprehensive knowing.

topics.headline: knowledge formula and surah thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this closing knowledge phrase begins a Surah 12 pattern at 12:50, 12:55, 12:76, 12:83, and 12:100 in which hidden motives and schemes are placed under divine knowledge.
topics.reason: Formula and recurrence rows, including 12:50, 12:55, 12:76, 12:83, and 12:100, are valid provenance but do not override the local predicate relation.

words.gloss_range: preposition that scopes the knowledge predicate toward its relative-clause object
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) prevents the knowledge predicate from remaining abstract. Joined into {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}), it turns {{ar:عَلِيمٌ}} ({{tr:ʿalīmun}}) toward the domain of what they do, making the closing attribute govern a concrete action-scope phrase.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the fused preposition and relative pronoun forming the knowledge-scope phrase
the knowledge predicate governed toward its object-domain

topics.headline: knowledge-scope preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine knowledge is directed specifically to the field of human action.
topics.reason: The preposition attaches to the knowledge predicate and fuses with the relative pronoun to form the governed scope phrase.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun broadening the object-domain to what or whatever they do
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) heads the relative clause and broadens the scope beyond a single named act. In {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}), it makes divine knowledge cover this concealment and the wider field of whatever the actors do.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the fused preposition and relative pronoun that opens the scope phrase

topics.headline: relative-scope broadening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closing clause expand from the hidden commodity act to an open domain of deeds.
topics.reason: The particle is parsed as relative, not interrogative or negative, and supplies the object-domain for the knowledge predicate.

words.gloss_range: imperfect plural doing: ongoing purposeful action by a plural set of actors under divine knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:يَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:yaʿmalūna}}) closes the ayah by shifting from completed narrative verbs to ongoing plural doing. The plural ending keeps the accountable actors collective, while the imperfect and relative scope make the phrase more than what they did once: it covers what they do as purposeful action. Thus concealment and commodification are absorbed into the wider field of deeds known by God, and later Joseph scenes at 12:69 and 12:89 return to action-accountability language.
words.root_gloss_range: doing, working, acting, practicing, and purposeful deeds; local Form I imperfect gives a broad action category

topics.headline: ongoing plural action scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the close is not limited to one past event but opens onto ongoing action.
topics.reason: The imperfect plural verb inside the relative clause contrasts with the preceding perfect verbs and broadens the action-domain.

topics.headline: purposeful deeds under knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees hiding and trade treated as accountable deeds, not accidental happenings.
topics.reason: The action root and God-plus-action accountability field fit the final divine knowledge clause.

topics.headline: surah action echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that later Joseph scenes return to action-accountability language, especially 12:69 and 12:89.
topics.reason: The same root and formulaic patterns are useful echoes, while the local verb remains the final relative-clause predicate governed by divine knowledge.
